correctness.rationale: For either G-leading directive, the unprimed denominators start q_0=1, q_1=a_1 and stay odd because each later partial quotient is 2. The modified endpoints Q_N=q'_N are not the parity selectors: Q_1 is even. Thus Theorem 54 takes the G-leading, both-unprimed-denominators-odd, a_{N+2}>1 branch, including N=0, and gives R_v(n+1)=n+3Q_{N+1}+Q_N for Q_N≤n<Q_{N+1}. Its Q recurrence has roots 1±√2 with a nonzero dominant coefficient for either a_1. Writing m=n+1 turns the block into Q_N+1≤m≤Q_{N+1}. The mesh m/Q_N has spacing 1/Q_N and endpoints tending to 1 and α=1+√2, so its cluster set is [1,α]. On it the ratio is 1+(3Q_{N+1}/Q_N+1−1/Q_N)/(m/Q_N). Compactness excludes all other limits, and rounded, clipped integer arguments attain each x in the limiting interval. The decreasing map 1+(3α+1)/x gives endpoints 3+√2 and 5+3√2. The excluded initial length m=1 does not affect the limit set. The record, certificate, and verifier were inspected. The verifier was not run, and its parity assertion on line 26 is tautological; the branch was instead checked directly from the primary theorem.
residual_risks: The supplied code is finite regression evidence for the formulas, not an independent calculation of all R_v(m) or a parity certificate.

value.rationale: The invariant and the extremal pair are natural, and reporting the full cluster set is more informative than reporting only the limsup. But the exact full interval is mechanically recoverable from the published all-length recurrence theorem via the limiting integer mesh. There is no independent residual invariant, example separating the two languages, or structural result. The calculation is useful exposition of the published theorem, not a distinct exact contribution under this standard.
